text:
A: Hiya. Erm, can you hear me?
B: Yeah. Hi.
A: I'm Gemma.
B: Gareth.
A: *(pause)* Where are you, then?
B: Basingstoke.
A: Oh, right. I'm Walsall. Bloxwich.
B: Right.
A: *(laughs)* Sorry, I'm not very good at these.
B: No, me neither. That's fine.
A: Have you done many?
B: This is the third. The last two did most of the talking, to be honest.
A: Same. Well, my first one was nice, he was easy. Erm. What do you do?
B: Structural engineer. Warehouses mainly.
A: Oh, I work in one. Well, a depot. Parcel sorting, off the M6. I run the late shift.
B: Big shed? Steel portal frame, probably.
A: I don't know, to be fair. It's big. It's got a big roof. *(laughs)*
B: Yeah, that'll be it. Most of them are. I've probably done one like it. You spend weeks on the calcs and then you drive past it and it's just a big grey box.
A: Does it not feel weird, though? Like, you know it's your one?
B: Bit, yeah. The kids don't care. I point and they don't look up.
A: How old are they?
B: Fifteen and twelve.
A: Is that their school shirts behind you? On the airer?
B: *(laughs)* Yeah. Ironing's not happening.
A: Mine's the same, I just hang stuff up and hope. Craig does most of the tea on my shift days, my husband. I do four long shifts a week, so by the end I'm knackered, I can't even think.
B: Late finish?
A: Gone eleven, sometimes later. And then I can't sleep straight after, so I'm sat up with Dolly. That's her, the ear in the corner.
B: Ah. What is she?
A: Staffie. She's twelve, her hips have gone a bit. The vet bills, honestly.
B: Yeah. Bonnie's getting there. Labrador cross. She was the kids' dog really, but it's me walks her.
A: That's always how it goes, isn't it.
B: Pretty much, yeah. *(pause)* I'm on my own with them, mostly. Their mum's in Reading.
A: Oh. That's a lot on you, though, with work as well.
B: Sort of, yeah. I muddle through. Forgot non-uniform day last week.
A: *(laughs)* Oh no. My mum did that to me once and I've never let her forget it.
B: Ellie won't let me forget it either.
A: Ellie, that's funny, the bloke I just spoke to, his daughter's called Ellie.
B: Popular one. *(pause)* Do you like it, then? Running the shift?
A: Erm. I like the people, most of them. I don't like the paperwork. Or when you have to let someone go, I lie awake over that. Sorry, does that answer it?
B: Yeah. I'm the same with paperwork. Timesheets.
A: My team leader chases mine, to be fair. I'd be lost without her.
B: Probably need one of those.
A: Everyone needs one of those. *(laughs)* Would you go back to the office full-time, if they—
